Personality traits shape how a character is expected to act, and acting against them causes stress. Some traits are congenital and can pass to children. Vanilla uses it very often.

label: Travel
summary: The game concept Travel: how a character gets from one place to another, mostly to attend activities.
details: In a text, `[travel|E]` shows the word "Travel" linked to the concept's explanation. A journey can be planned by hiring a travel leader, picking travel options and shaping the route. On the way the traveler meets other characters and may face danger. Vanilla uses it often.

label: Danger
summary: The game concept Danger: the risks of passing through hazardous lands, such as deserts or swamps, while traveling.
details: In a text, `[travel_danger|E]` shows the word "Danger" linked to the concept's explanation. Raising travel safety, through travel options or a travel leader, lowers the risk, and some cultural traditions reduce or remove certain kinds of danger.

label: Danger
summary: The icon of the game concept Danger: the risks of passing through hazardous lands while traveling.
details: In a text, `[travel_danger_i|E]` shows the travel danger icon linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla writes `[travel_danger_i]` without `|E`, as a bare icon next to a danger value.

label: Destination
summary: Another name of the game concept Destination: the goal of a journey, or one of its goals.
details: In a text, `[travel_destination|E]` shows the words "Travel Destination" linked to the concept's explanation. For a pilgrimage it is the holy site; on a tour every vassal visited is a destination.

label: Travel option
summary: The game concept Travel Option: a choice made while planning a journey that improves or changes it.
details: In a text, `[travel_option|E]` shows the words "Travel Option" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it often in texts about the options' effects.

details: In a text, `[travel_options|E]` shows the words "Travel Options" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Safety
summary: The game concept Safety: a traveler's protection against the dangers of a journey.
details: In a text, `[travel_safety|E]` shows the word "Safety" linked to the concept's explanation. A high value helps avoid danger. It depends on the traveler's skills and on those of their travel leader.

label: Speed
summary: The game concept Speed: how fast a traveler moves, so how soon they reach their destination.
details: In a text, `[travel_speed|E]` shows the word "Speed" linked to the concept's explanation. It depends on the traveler's skills and on those of their travel leader.

label: Travel
summary: Another form of the game concept Travel: how a character gets from one place to another, mostly to attend activities.
details: In a text, `[traveled|E]` shows the word "Traveled" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Treasury
summary: The game concept Treasury: in some governments, funds that may only be spent on government purposes, apart from the ruler's personal gold.
details: In a text, `[treasury|E]` shows the word "Treasury" linked to the concept's explanation. It is built up centrally by the top liege or locally; part of the tax income turns into treasury, and a vassal may receive treasury from their liege based on taxes and other obligations. A ruler can move gold into it at will. The treasury stays with the title when the title gets a new holder.

label: Treasury budgeting
summary: Another name of the game concept Treasury Budgeting: the system that hands out central treasury to chosen vassals and sub-vassals at set rates.
details: In a text, `[treasury_budget|E]` shows the words "Treasury Budget" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in many treasury and ministry texts.

label: Budget base rate
summary: The game concept Budget Base Rate: what a standard recipient of a budget category receives.
details: In a text, `[treasury_budget_base_rate|E]` shows the words "Budget Base Rate" linked to the concept's explanation. A recipient can get more or less than this depending on their rank, merit level or other modifiers.

label: Budget base rate
summary: A short name of the game concept Budget Base Rate: what a standard recipient of a budget category receives.
details: In a text, `[treasury_budget_base_rate_short|E]` shows the words "Base Rate" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in breakdown entries and modifier names for the monthly budget amounts.

label: Budget capacity
summary: The game concept Budget Capacity: the treasury available each month for budgeting.
details: In a text, `[treasury_budget_capacity|E]` shows the words "Budget Capacity" linked to the concept's explanation. It is the treasury income minus regular costs that budgeting does not handle, such as vassal development and court amenities.

label: Budget category
summary: The game concept Budget Category: one part of treasury budgeting that can be given a share of the budget.
details: In a text, `[treasury_budget_category|E]` shows the words "Budget Category" linked to the concept's explanation. Each category can have its own recipients, and some pay out gold instead of treasury.

label: Budget category trend
summary: The game concept Budget Category Trend: how much more or less treasury a budget category gets than at the previous budget.
details: In a text, `[treasury_budget_category_trend|E]` shows the words "Budget Category Trend" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this name; vanilla writes the short form.

label: Budget category trend
summary: A short name of the game concept Budget Category Trend: how much more or less treasury a budget category gets than at the previous budget.
details: In a text, `[treasury_budget_category_trend_short|E]` shows the word "Trend" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it as a column header in the treasury budget window.

label: Treasury budget deficit
summary: The game concept Treasury Budget Deficit: when a budget spends more than the budget capacity, the excess is taken from the monthly treasury income.
details: In a text, `[treasury_budget_deficit|E]` shows the words "Treasury Budget Deficit" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this name; vanilla writes the short form.

label: Treasury budget deficit
summary: A short name of the game concept Treasury Budget Deficit: when a budget spends more than the budget capacity, the excess is taken from the monthly treasury income.
details: In a text, `[treasury_budget_deficit_short|E]` shows the word "Deficit" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the treasury budget window's summary.

label: Unallocated treasury budget
summary: The game concept Unallocated Treasury Budget: budget left unassigned, which goes into the general treasury income.
details: In a text, `[treasury_budget_unallocated|E]` shows the words "Unallocated Treasury Budget" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this name; vanilla writes the short form.

label: Unallocated treasury budget
summary: A short name of the game concept Unallocated Treasury Budget: budget left unassigned, which goes into the general treasury income.
details: In a text, `[treasury_budget_unallocated_short|E]` shows the word "Unallocated" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the treasury budget window's summary.

label: Treasury budgeting
summary: The game concept Treasury Budgeting: the system that hands out central treasury to chosen vassals and sub-vassals at set rates.
details: In a text, `[treasury_budgeting|E]` shows the words "Treasury Budgeting" linked to the concept's explanation. When a budget is enacted, a base rate per vassal is worked out for each budget category from the budget capacity. That base rate stays fixed until the next budget, so more recipients mean higher costs.

label: Cardinal budget
summary: The game concept Cardinal Budget: treasury that the central church treasury gives to cardinals.
details: In a text, `[treasury_cardinal_budget|E]` shows the words "Cardinal Budget" linked to the concept's explanation. It stands for the benefices (church incomes) assigned to them, directly or indirectly.

label: Cardinal budget
summary: Another name of the game concept Cardinal Budget: treasury that the central church treasury gives to cardinals.
details: In a text, `[treasury_cardinal_budget_benefices|E]` shows the words "Cardinal Benefices" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it as the name of the church benefices law.

label: Cardinal budget
summary: A short name of the game concept Cardinal Budget: treasury that the central church treasury gives to cardinals.
details: In a text, `[treasury_cardinal_budget_short|E]` shows the word "Cardinal" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the modifier name for the monthly treasury from the cardinal budget.

label: Treasury debt
summary: The game concept Treasury Debt: having less than zero treasury.
details: In a text, `[treasury_debt|E]` shows the words "Treasury Debt" linked to the concept's explanation. It usually comes from hiring mercenaries without enough treasury, long wars, or paying more salaries than the vassals bring in. In debt a ruler cannot declare new wars, treasury-funded men-at-arms do not reinforce and enemies get an advantage in battle. The deeper the debt, the bigger the penalties: fewer levies, lower county opinion and lower vassal opinion. Minor events can also follow, such as corruption in domain counties.

label: Treasury
summary: The icon of the game concept Treasury: in some governments, funds that may only be spent on government purposes.
details: In a text, `[treasury_i|E]` shows the treasury icon linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla often writes `[treasury_i]` without `|E`, as a bare icon in front of an amount.

label: Military budget
summary: The game concept Military Budget: treasury the central government sends to vassals holding military provinces, to pay for extra military activity.
details: In a text, `[treasury_military_budget|E]` shows the words "Military Budget" linked to the concept's explanation. The amount comes from the periodic allocation of the top liege's treasury income.

label: Military budget
summary: A short name of the game concept Military Budget: treasury the central government sends to vassals holding military provinces.
details: In a text, `[treasury_military_budget_short|E]` shows the word "Military" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in budget focus texts and in a monthly treasury modifier name.

label: Ministry budget
summary: The game concept Ministry Budget: treasury the central government sends to vassals to fund ministries.
details: In a text, `[treasury_ministry_budget|E]` shows the words "Ministry Budget" linked to the concept's explanation. The amount comes from the periodic allocation of the top liege's treasury income.

details: In a text, `[treasury_ministry_budget_short|E]` shows the word "Ministry" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in budget focus texts and in a monthly treasury modifier name.

summary: The game concept Salary Budget: treasury the central government sends to vassals, who receive it as gold for their personal salary.
details: In a text, `[treasury_salary_budget|E]` shows the words "Salary Budget" linked to the concept's explanation. The amount comes from the periodic allocation of the top liege's treasury income.

summary: A short name of the game concept Salary Budget: treasury the central government sends to vassals as gold for their personal salary.
details: In a text, `[treasury_salary_budget_short|E]` shows the word "Salary" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in budget focus texts and in a monthly treasury modifier name.

summary: The game concept Vassal Development: treasury sent to direct vassals through their liege, based on their tax contributions and other obligations.
details: In a text, `[treasury_vassal_development|E]` shows the words "Vassal Development" linked to the concept's explanation. It is one of the regular costs that budgeting does not manage.

label: Trial-by-combat
summary: The game concept Trial-by-Combat: in some cultures, a dispute that words or war cannot settle is decided by a single combat duel.
details: In a text, `[trial_by_combat|E]` shows the word "Trial-by-Combat" linked to the concept's explanation. The two characters fight for a settlement chosen beforehand; if the accused wins, they are proven innocent. Both must be of a valid culture, the challenger uses up an imprisonment reason against the other, and the other may not be their liege, vassal, or a guest or courtier of them or their vassals. A ruler unfit to fight can name a knight; a fight to the death is only possible when the wronged party is tribal and both fight in person.

label: Trial-by-combat

details: In a text, `[trial_by_combat_combat|E]` shows the word "Combat" linked to the concept's explanation; the concept's own description uses this form. No other vanilla text uses it.

label: Tribal
summary: The game concept Tribal: the tribal government form.
details: In a text, `[tribal|E]` shows the word "Tribal" linked to the concept's explanation. Tribal realms have held-back county development, cannot get past Tribal Era innovations, cannot build new holdings and usually cannot change their succession law. In return they can spend prestige instead of gold on building and hiring men-at-arms and have more casus belli than feudal realms. Armies that are not tribal suffer a supply limit penalty in hostile tribal land.

label: Tribal authority
summary: The game concept Tribal Authority: how much power a tribal ruler holds over their vassals.
details: In a text, `[tribal_authority|E]` shows the words "Tribal Authority" linked to the concept's explanation. Compared with crown authority it gives fewer powers, and at later levels. It has four levels: disparate tribes, limited, high and absolute tribal authority.

label: Tribal
summary: Another name of the game concept Tribal: the tribal government form.
details: In a text, `[tribal_government|E]` shows the words "Tribal Government" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Tribal holding
summary: The game concept Tribal Holding: a tribe, a kind of holding that gives little tax but many levies, prestige and men-at-arms upgrades.
details: In a text, `[tribal_holding|E]` shows the words "Tribal Holding" linked to the concept's explanation. Tribes can be upgraded only a little and are strong early but fall behind over time. Only tribal characters can hold them without penalties. While a tribe exists in a county no other holdings can be built there; feudal rulers must pay gold to turn tribes into castles.

label: Tribal holding
summary: The plural of the game concept Tribal Holding: tribes, holdings that give little tax but many levies, prestige and men-at-arms upgrades.
details: In a text, `[tribal_holdings|E]` shows the words "Tribal Holdings" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Tribal
summary: The icon of the game concept Tribal: the tribal government form.

label: Tribal holding
summary: Another name of the game concept Tribal Holding: a tribe, a kind of holding that gives little tax but many levies, prestige and men-at-arms upgrades.
details: In a text, `[tribe|E]` shows the word "Tribe" linked to the concept's explanation.

summary: Another name, in the plural, of the game concept Tribal Holding: tribes, holdings that give little tax but many levies, prestige and men-at-arms upgrades.
details: In a text, `[tribes|E]` shows the word "Tribes" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Tributary
summary: The plural of the game concept Tributary: rulers who have an agreement with another ruler, their suzerain, and pay them tribute.
details: In a text, `[tributaries|E]` shows the word "Tributaries" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it very often.

label: Tributary
summary: The game concept Tributary: a ruler who has an agreement with another ruler, their suzerain, and pays them tribute.
details: In a text, `[tributary|E]` shows the word "Tributary" linked to the concept's explanation. The tribute is paid regularly in herd, taxes, prestige or piety depending on the type, and the tributary gets a truce with the suzerain in return. Tributaries are a looser kind of subject: they cannot join factions but can break free if the requirements are not met, and they break free soon after the suzerain is neither landed nor migrating.

label: Tributary contract
summary: The game concept Tributary Contract: the obligations between a tributary and their suzerain.
details: In a text, `[tributary_contract|E]` shows the words "Tributary Contract" linked to the concept's explanation. The obligations are negotiated for each tributary separately. Based on them a tributary pays a share of their taxes, levies, herd, prestige or piety to the suzerain.

label: Tributary contract
summary: The plural of the game concept Tributary Contract: the obligations between tributaries and their suzerain.
details: In a text, `[tributary_contracts|E]` shows the words "Tributary Contracts" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

details: In a text, `[tributary_possessive|E]` shows the word "Tributary's" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in concept and government texts, for example about a tributary's capital holding.

label: Tributary taxes

details: In a text, `[tributary_taxes|E]` shows the words "Tributary Taxes" linked to the concept's explanation. The amount depends on each tributary's obligations. Seen from the tributary, the same taxes are called suzerain taxes, to tell them apart from tributary taxes the tributary collects from its own tributaries.

label: Tribute mission
summary: Another name of the game concept Tribute Mission: a tributary has to pay respects and tribute to their suzerain at regular times.
details: In a text, `[tribute|E]` shows the word "Tribute" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it often.

label: Tribute mission
summary: The game concept Tribute Mission: a tributary has to pay respects and tribute to their suzerain at regular times.
details: In a text, `[tribute_mission|E]` shows the words "Tribute Mission" linked to the concept's explanation. Failing to do so can have various consequences, the mildest being a loss of legitimacy.

label: Tribute mission
summary: The plural of the game concept Tribute Mission: a tributary has to pay respects and tribute to their suzerain at regular times.
details: In a text, `[tribute_missions|E]` shows the words "Tribute Missions" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Tribute mission
summary: Another name, in the plural, of the game concept Tribute Mission: a tributary has to pay respects and tribute to their suzerain at regular times.

details: In a text, `[trilateral_interaction|E]` shows the words "Trilateral Interaction" linked to the concept's explanation. One example is a diarch's powers, which a liege can block with a regency veto. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Trilateral interaction
summary: The plural of the game concept Trilateral Interaction: interactions that need the approval of a third party as well as of the recipient.

details: In a text, `[tyranny|E]` shows the word "Tyranny" linked to the concept's explanation. For example, imprisoning someone who has committed no crime, or revoking their titles, is tyrannical. Tyranny works as an opinion penalty with every character in the realm. Vanilla uses it often.

label: Tyranny

details: In a text, `[unassigned_vassal|E]` shows the words "Untaxed Vassals" linked to the concept's explanation. Once assigned to a tax jurisdiction that has a tax collector, they start paying every month. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Untaxed vassals
summary: A short name of the game concept Untaxed Vassals: clan vassals who are not assigned as taxpayers to a tax jurisdiction, so pay no taxes or levies.
details: In a text, `[unassigned_vassal_short|E]` shows the word "Untaxed" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Untaxed vassals
summary: Another name of the game concept Untaxed Vassals: clan vassals who are not assigned to any tax jurisdiction, so they pay no taxes and give no levies.
details: In a text, `[unassigned_vassals|E]` shows "Untaxed Vassals" linked to the concept's explanation. Once such a vassal is assigned to a tax jurisdiction that has a tax collector, they start paying every month. Vanilla uses it in the tax collector window, for example in the warning that counts how many such vassals you have.

label: Title creation
summary: Another name of the game concept Title Creation: a ruler who controls most of the de jure land of a title nobody holds yet can create that title.
details: In a text, `[uncreated_title|E]` shows "Uncreated Title" linked to the Title Creation explanation. Creating a title costs gold and gives prestige; only duchies, kingdoms and empires can be created. Vanilla uses it in a concept text about a casus belli that seizes the counties needed to create a duchy.

label: Undirected great holy war
summary: The game concept Undirected Great Holy War: a holy war that a head of faith declares to bring a kingdom under the rule of their faith.
details: In a text, `[undirected_great_holy_war|E]` shows "Undirected Great Holy War" linked to the concept's explanation. Such a war does not start at once but first goes through a preparation phase, during which rulers of the attacking faith can donate gold to the war chest. If the attackers win, the targeted kingdom is taken and handed to a character of their faith. Vanilla uses it in the decision that launches one and in the preparation phase concept.

label: Undirected great holy war
summary: The plural name of the game concept Undirected Great Holy War: a holy war that a head of faith declares to bring a kingdom under the rule of their faith.
details: In a text, `[undirected_great_holy_wars|E]` shows "Undirected Great Holy Wars" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the concept texts about great holy wars and the war chest.

label: House unity
summary: Another name of the game concept House Unity: how well the members of a clan house get along and how they feel about each other.
details: In a text, `[unity|E]` shows "Unity" linked to the House Unity explanation. House unity has several levels, each with benefits and penalties for the house's members; unifying actions between members raise it and divisive ones lower it. Vanilla uses it where the house head steers unity.

label: Unknown
summary: The game concept Unknown: the tenet status of a core tenet or doctrine that a rite knows nothing about.
details: In a text, `[unknown_tenet_status|E]` shows "Unknown" linked to the concept's explanation. Followers of the rite do not know the tenet or doctrine and cannot pick it when making a new rite or as a personal tenet. Vanilla uses it in the faith view and in the concept text that lists the possible tenet stances.

label: Unlanded
summary: The game concept Unlanded: characters who have no holdings in their domain.
details: In a text, `[unlanded|E]` shows "Unlanded" linked to the concept's explanation. Unlanded characters can still be rulers of a kind, for example heads of faith and grand masters of holy orders. Vanilla uses it often, for example for courtiers and for elective succession candidates.

label: Unmanaged holdings
summary: The singular name of the game concept Unmanaged Holdings: disabled holdings that do not count toward the domain limit.
details: In a text, `[unmanaged_holding|E]` shows "Unmanaged Holding" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this name; vanilla writes `[unmanaged_holdings|E]`.

label: Unmanaged holdings
summary: The game concept Unmanaged Holdings: disabled holdings that do not count toward the domain limit (how many holdings a ruler can keep in their own domain).
details: In a text, `[unmanaged_holdings|E]` shows "Unmanaged Holdings" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it as a header in the realm window's domain limit part.

label: Unpredictable icon
summary: The icon of the game concept Unpredictable, the AI economic personality of a ruler with no traits pushing them toward any particular economic strategy.
details: This alias's text is an icon (`@unpredictable_icon!`), not a word, so `[unpredictable_i]` shows the icon. Vanilla writes it without `|E` in front of the personality's name. Such a ruler may spend heavily on buildings for a while or save gold slowly, and goes to war at a regular pace.

label: Vassal stance
summary: Another name of the game concept Vassal Stance; the concept lists it among its names, with the preferred and unpreferred heirs.
details: In a text, `[unpreferred_heir|E]` shows "Unpreferred Heir" linked to the Vassal Stance explanation. Each vassal has a stance that shapes their opinion of their liege and which heir they want as successor; each stance prefers one heir. Vanilla uses it as a reason for joining a faction: the liege was an unpreferred heir.

label: Vassal stance
summary: Another name, in the plural, of the game concept Vassal Stance; the concept lists it among its names, with the preferred and unpreferred heirs.
details: In a text, `[unpreferred_heirs|E]` shows "Unpreferred Heirs" linked to the Vassal Stance explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Unpressed claim
summary: Another name of the game concept Unpressed Claim: a weak claim that the claimant's children do not inherit.
details: In a text, `[unpressed|E]` shows "Unpressed" linked to the Unpressed Claim explanation. An unpressed claim becomes pressed once it is used in a casus belli to declare war, even if that war ends in a white peace. No vanilla text uses this name with `|E`.

label: Unpressed claim
summary: The game concept Unpressed Claim: a legally weak claim on a title that the claimant's children do not inherit.
details: In a text, `[unpressed_claim|E]` shows "Unpressed Claim" linked to the concept's explanation. Using the claim in a casus belli to declare war turns it into a pressed claim, even if the war ends in a white peace. Vanilla uses it in effect texts such as "Gets an unpressed claim on ...".

label: Unpressed claim icon
summary: The icon of the game concept Unpressed Claim, a weak claim that the claimant's children do not inherit.
details: This alias's text is an icon (`@unpressed_claim!`), not a word, so `[unpressed_claim_i]` shows the icon. Vanilla writes it without `|E` right before the word: `[unpressed_claim_i][unpressed_claim|E]` in the character window and the title view.

label: Unpressed claim
summary: The plural name of the game concept Unpressed Claim: legally weak claims that the claimant's children do not inherit.
details: In a text, `[unpressed_claims|E]` shows "Unpressed Claims" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in concept texts, for example: pressed claims are inherited by children as unpressed claims, and claims can be bought as unpressed claims for piety.

label: Unreformed pagan combat advantage
summary: The game concept Unreformed Pagan Combat Advantage: unreformed pagan faiths get a battle advantage in counties of their own faith.
details: In a text, `[unreformed_pagan_combat_bonus|E]` shows "Unreformed Pagan Combat Advantage" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it as the name of the unreformed faith province modifier and in the list of what the unreformed doctrine grants.

label: Unrestricted
summary: The game concept Unrestricted: the highest level of nomadic authority, which only one character in the whole game can reach.
details: In a text, `[unrestricted_nomadic|E]` shows "Unrestricted" linked to the concept's explanation. The character who reaches it becomes the Greatest of Khans, and independent rulers at this level can use the decisions to become Greatest of Khans and to conquer the world. Vanilla lists it among the five nomadic authority levels.

label: Unruly nomads
summary: The game concept Unruly Nomads: the lowest level of nomadic authority.
details: In a text, `[unruly_nomadic|E]` shows "Unruly Nomads" linked to the concept's explanation. At this level, migration can only target de jure counties inside the Great Steppe, and characters cannot be imprisoned. Vanilla lists it first among the five nomadic authority levels.

label: Untaxed jurisdiction
summary: The game concept Untaxed Jurisdiction: a tax jurisdiction that has taxpayers but no tax collector, so its taxpayers give their liege no taxes or levies.
details: In a text, `[untaxed_jurisdiction|E]` shows "Untaxed Jurisdiction" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses the singular name; vanilla writes `[untaxed_jurisdictions|E]`.

label: Untaxed jurisdiction
summary: A short name of the game concept Untaxed Jurisdiction: a tax jurisdiction with taxpayers but no tax collector, which yields no taxes or levies.
details: In a text, `[untaxed_jurisdiction_short|E]` shows just "Untaxed" linked to the Untaxed Jurisdiction explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Untaxed jurisdiction
summary: The plural name of the game concept Untaxed Jurisdiction: tax jurisdictions with taxpayers but no tax collector, which yield no taxes or levies.
details: In a text, `[untaxed_jurisdictions|E]` shows "Untaxed Jurisdictions" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the tax collector warning that counts how many such jurisdictions you have.

label: Usurp title
summary: Another name of the game concept Usurp Title: taking a title from a foreign ruler when more than half of its de jure counties are in your realm.
details: In a text, `[usurp|E]` shows "Usurp" linked to the Usurp Title explanation. Usurping gives you the title, which matters for being the rightful liege of your vassals; it is harder when the holder's faith is hostile to yours. Vanilla uses it in concept texts (co-rulers usurping) and in the important action that says you can usurp a title.

label: Usurp title
summary: The game concept Usurp Title: a title held by a foreign ruler can usually be taken over when more than 50% of its de jure counties are inside your realm.
details: In a text, `[usurp_title|E]` shows "Usurp Title" linked to the concept's explanation. The title passes to you, which matters for being the rightful liege of your vassals. If the holder's faith is hostile to yours, you can only usurp once the holder has none of the title's de jure counties left in their realm. No vanilla text uses this name; vanilla writes `[usurp|E]`.

label: Usurp title
summary: Another name of the game concept Usurp Title, the noun for taking over a foreign ruler's title when most of its de jure counties are in your realm.
details: In a text, `[usurpation|E]` shows "Usurpation" linked to the Usurp Title explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Usurp title
summary: Another name of the game concept Usurp Title, the past form for a title taken over from a foreign ruler.
details: In a text, `[usurped|E]` shows "Usurped" linked to the Usurp Title explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Valuable prisoner
summary: The game concept Valuable Prisoner: a prisoner who gives war score when captured during a war.
details: In a text, `[valuable_prisoner|E]` shows "Valuable Prisoner" linked to the concept's explanation. A character counts as one if they are third in line or closer to inherit their war leader's primary title. Unlike prisoners of war, valuable prisoners are released when the war ends. Vanilla's combat events also save the captured character as `scope:valuable_prisoner` (`[valuable_prisoner.GetTitledFirstName]`); those uses are of that saved scope, not of this concept.

label: Valuable prisoner
summary: The plural name of the game concept Valuable Prisoner: prisoners who give war score when captured during a war.
details: In a text, `[valuable_prisoners|E]` shows "Valuable Prisoners" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in concept texts and in the note that valuable prisoners taken by all war participants are released at the end of the war.

label: Varangian adventure
summary: The game concept Varangian Adventure: a special war in which the attacker means to move their whole realm to the war target.
details: In a text, `[varangian_adventure|E]` shows "Varangian Adventure" linked to the concept's explanation. A winner annexes the target counties at once and moves their capital there; their old vassals become independent and their old counties go to new local warlords. Only duke and count tier rulers can use it. Vanilla uses it as the casus belli's name and in a cultural innovation that unlocks it.

label: Varangian adventure
summary: A short name of the game concept Varangian Adventure, a war in which the attacker moves their whole realm to the war target.
details: In a text, `[varangian_adventure_adventure|E]` shows just "Adventure" linked to the Varangian Adventure explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Varangian adventure
summary: The plural name of the game concept Varangian Adventure, wars in which the attacker moves their whole realm to the war target.
details: In a text, `[varangian_adventures|E]` shows "Varangian Adventures" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in a game rule's description.

label: Varangian adventure
summary: Another name of the game concept Varangian Adventure, for being on such a war, in which the attacker moves their whole realm to the war target.
details: In a text, `[varangian_adventuring|E]` shows "Adventuring" linked to the Varangian Adventure explanation. Vanilla uses it in an effect text about extra troops above the cap while adventuring.

label: Vassal
summary: The game concept Vassal: a ruler who has sworn fealty to another ruler, their liege.
details: In a text, `[vassal|E]` shows "Vassal" linked to the concept's explanation. A vassal owes their liege levies and taxes (their obligations) and gets protection in return. A vassal with low opinion of their liege may join factions or scheme to replace them. Vanilla uses it very often.

label: Vassal contract
summary: The game concept Vassal Contract: the agreement that sets the obligations between a vassal and their liege.
details: In a text, `[vassal_contract|E]` shows "Vassal Contract" linked to the concept's explanation. Feudal, clan, administrative and nomadic vassals have different obligations, agreed separately for each vassal, and every vassal pays a share of their taxes and levies to the liege based on them. Vanilla uses it in an achievement and in effect and interaction texts about improving or worsening a contract.

label: Vassal contract
summary: The plural name of the game concept Vassal Contract, the agreements that set the obligations between vassals and their liege.
details: In a text, `[vassal_contracts|E]` shows "Vassal Contracts" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in concept texts and important actions about changing contracts.

label: Vassal directive
summary: The game concept Vassal Directive: an order a liege gives a vassal that steers their councillor tasks and which buildings they build.
details: In a text, `[vassal_directive|E]` shows "Vassal Directive" linked to the concept's explanation. A directive must first be enabled, for example by having 50 or more opinion with the vassal; advanced government forms do not need this. Vanilla uses it in the administrative vassal window.

label: Vassal directive
summary: The plural name of the game concept Vassal Directive, orders a liege gives vassals about their councillor tasks and buildings.
details: In a text, `[vassal_directives|E]` shows "Vassal Directives" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Vassal limit
summary: The game concept Vassal Limit: how many direct vassals a ruler can have without penalty, not counting baron tier vassals.
details: In a text, `[vassal_limit|E]` shows "Vassal Limit" linked to the concept's explanation. Going above it is allowed but lowers the taxes and levies the vassals give, so handing some vassals on can be better. Vanilla uses it in the warning shown when you are above the limit.

label: Subject obligations
summary: The game concept Subject Obligations: how much tax and how many levies a subject gives their suzerain.
details: In a text, `[vassal_obligations|E]` shows "Subject Obligations" linked to the concept's explanation. The subject's government form decides how the obligations are set; for feudal and clan vassals they come from the vassal contract. Vanilla uses it in an interaction that offers increased obligations in exchange for land.

label: Vassal
summary: The possessive form of the game concept Vassal, a ruler who has sworn fealty to a liege.
details: In a text, `[vassal_possessive|E]` shows "Vassal's" linked to the Vassal explanation. Vanilla uses it in a few interaction and situation texts.

label: Vassal stance
summary: The game concept Vassal Stance: the attitude every vassal has, which shapes their opinion of their liege and which heir they want as successor.
details: In a text, `[vassal_stance|E]` shows "Vassal Stance" linked to the concept's explanation. Vassals with the same stance like and dislike the same things, for example glory hounds dislike it when you lose wars. Each stance prefers one heir; vanilla uses it in AI personality tooltips and the my realm window's filter.

label: Vassal stance
summary: The plural name of the game concept Vassal Stance, the attitudes that shape vassals' opinion of their liege and their preferred heir.
details: In a text, `[vassal_stances|E]` shows "Vassal Stances" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the my realm window, for example "Preferred by these vassal stances".

label: Vassal taxes
summary: The game concept Vassal Taxes: the taxes a ruler receives from their vassals.
details: In a text, `[vassal_taxes|E]` shows "Vassal Taxes" linked to the concept's explanation. The amount depends on each vassal's obligations. Seen from the vassal's side, the same taxes are called liege taxes. Vanilla uses it for the tax from vassals line.

label: Vassal
summary: Another name of the game concept Vassal, for the bond of a ruler who has sworn fealty to a liege.
details: In a text, `[vassalage|E]` shows "Vassalage" linked to the Vassal explanation. Vanilla uses it in concept texts, for example the interaction that offers vassalage to another ruler.

label: Vassal
summary: Another name of the game concept Vassal, for making a ruler someone's vassal.
details: In a text, `[vassalization|E]` shows "Vassalization" linked to the Vassal explanation. Vanilla uses it in concept texts, for example the casus belli for forced vassalization.

label: Forced vassalization casus belli
summary: Another name of the game concept Forced Vassalization Casus Belli: a reason for war that forces a neighbouring independent ruler of lower rank to become your vassal.
details: In a text, `[vassalization_casus_belli|E]` shows "Forced Vassalization" linked to the concept's explanation. The Forced Vassalage perk unlocks it, and the target may hold only up to a set number of counties. Vanilla uses it in the war's name, "Forced Vassalization of ...".

label: Vassal
summary: Another name of the game concept Vassal, the verb for making a ruler your vassal.
details: In a text, `[vassalize|E]` shows "Vassalize" linked to the Vassal explanation. Vanilla uses it in important actions such as the note that you can vassalize neighbours.

label: Forced vassalization casus belli
summary: The game concept Forced Vassalization Casus Belli: a reason for war that forces a neighbouring independent ruler of lower rank to become your vassal.
details: In a text, `[vassalize_casus_belli|E]` shows "Forced Vassalization Casus Belli" linked to the concept's explanation. The Forced Vassalage perk unlocks it. You can only target a ruler whose realm has no more than a set number of counties, and that number can be raised. Vanilla uses it in effect texts that unlock or allow it.

label: Forced vassalization casus belli
summary: Another name of the game concept Forced Vassalization Casus Belli, for a ruler made a vassal by force.
details: In a text, `[vassalized_casus_belli|E]` shows "Forcefully Vassalized" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in an interaction text saying a character holds too many counties to be forcefully vassalized.

label: Vassal
summary: The plural name of the game concept Vassal, rulers who have sworn fealty to a liege.
details: In a text, `[vassals|E]` shows "Vassals" linked to the Vassal explanation. Vanilla uses it very often.

label: Vassal
summary: The plural possessive form of the game concept Vassal, rulers who have sworn fealty to a liege.
details: In a text, `[vassals_possessive|E]` shows "Vassals'" linked to the Vassal explanation. Vanilla uses it in government privilege texts, for example that the liege cannot revoke the vassals' titles.

label: Diarchy veto
summary: Another name of the game concept Diarchy Veto: when a diarch uses one of their diarch powers, their liege may stop it at a cost in prestige.
details: In a text, `[veto|E]` shows "Veto" linked to the Diarchy Veto explanation. Vanilla uses it in concept and tutorial texts about diarch powers.

label: Victim
summary: The game concept Victim: a child who is being harassed by another child, their bully.
details: In a text, `[victim|E]` shows "Victim" linked to the concept's explanation. On reaching adulthood the victim may become rivals with the bully, or leave it behind. Vanilla uses it in effect texts such as "Becomes ...'s victim".

label: Victim
summary: The possessive form of the game concept Victim, a child harassed by a bully.
details: In a text, `[victim_possessive|E]` shows "Victim's" linked to the Victim explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Victim
summary: The plural name of the game concept Victim, children harassed by a bully.
details: In a text, `[victims|E]` shows "Victims" linked to the Victim explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Victim
summary: The plural possessive form of the game concept Victim, children harassed by a bully.
details: In a text, `[victims_possessive|E]` shows "Victims'" linked to the Victim explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Victory
summary: The game concept Victory: one of the three ways a war can end, with the outcome set by the war's casus belli.
details: In a text, `[victory|E]` shows "Victory" linked to the concept's explanation. For the attacker it usually means taking titles in the war target's region; for the defender it usually means the attacker pays a large sum of gold as reparations. The other two endings are white peace and defeat.

label: Virtue
summary: The game concept Virtue: a trait that a rite considers virtuous.
details: In a text, `[virtue|E]` shows "Virtue" linked to the concept's explanation. Characters with such a trait get opinion bonuses from everyone who sees the trait as virtuous, even of another rite, and characters whose own rite sees their trait as virtuous gain extra piety every month. Which traits are virtues differs from rite to rite.

label: Virtue weight
summary: The game concept Virtue Weight: how strongly a rite treats a trait as virtuous, set by the rite's core tenets, doctrines and religion.
details: In a text, `[virtue_weight|E]` shows "Virtue Weight" linked to the concept's explanation. The traits with the highest virtue weight in a rite become its virtues (the same goes for sin weight and sins). Vanilla uses it in the trait tooltip line that shows the weight.
